name: Debris-Crown
specific_features: Satellite graveyard: a decaying halo of thousands of wrecks from the Concordance War—spy eyes, relay cores, and kinetic launch platforms—rains onto the dust seas in slow arcs, so that the whole surface is ringed with burn-scarred landing tracks pointing at the sky.

Signal of unknown origin: among the dead satellites, unit WITNESS-9 remains in a perfectly maintained orbit and broadcasts a fresh set of surface coordinates every day, though no nation of the Concordance survives to service it.
description: Debris-Crown turns slowly under a white-hot sun, its face a churned plain of grey dust and fused glass where falling satellites have struck for two centuries. Solar wind has combed the dust into long parallel ridges that run unbroken to the horizon. By day the sky is a hard black studded with the glint of the graveyard overhead; by night, meteor trails stitch it like falling rain.

There is no sound at all, no air to carry the hiss of cooling metal or the whisper of dust displaced by a boot. Heat soaks through suit gloves within minutes of sunrise, and every step throws up slow-arc curtains of powder that hang in the weak gravity. The silence presses harder than the heat.

The Concordance War ended here in effect if not in name: both fleets scuttled their orbital networks over this little world rather than let them be captured, and their wreckage has been sifting down ever since. Scavenger crews work the impact fields for intact sensor cores, walking lines of craters that read like a ledger of everything the war once watched. Yet one satellite never falls. WITNESS-9 holds its station with impossible precision and posts new coordinates each dawn.

The coordinates WITNESS-9 transmits have led diggers to buried command bunkers, lost pay vaults, and twice to mass graves—and always before anyone else knew those sites existed. Three salvage syndicates now shadow the satellite's ground track waiting for each day's broadcast, and at least one has tried to shoot it down. Every interceptor launched at it has simply stopped transmitting mid-flight, and no one has gone back for the footage.
